text: SA19-6 (Witt vectors, formal groups, Dieudonné rings; 43:37-38, 181-202) is used by SA19-1 (local Jacobians of curves through S_∞, 43:81-82; generalized Jacobians' unipotent parts) and by SA19-2 (the Greenberg realizations of G_a, W_n, and α_p, 43:112; the elementary types of 160-177).

SA19-1 (class field theory, generalized Jacobians, Rosenlicht theory; 43:2-35, 40-43, 80, 113, 206-208) is used by SA19-5 (local Jacobians as the local pieces of J_1 -> J_0, 43:18, 70-82) and by SA19-2 (the curve duality of 128-140 uses Pic and the Jacobian's self-duality, 133; item 9 of 102 is Serre's local class field theory).
SA19-5 (43:45-82) is used by SA19-2 through local duality on henselian schemes (43:89-90, 135-140).
SA19-2 (43:89-140, 160-170, 203-205) uses SA19-1 and SA19-6 as above and feeds SA18-11 (integral models and local duality: 43:117's statements (2), (3)).
SA19-14 (cote 44) uses SA19-1 (the generalized Albanese, 44:2, 44:9) and SA18-14 (duality of abelian varieties).

**Placement notes (sweep 2 against the pages).** 43:145-156 are placed under SA19-2 but are ℓ-adic Galois images ("algèbre de Serre", 147-156); 43:143-145 are Tate's text, not his; SA19-7's "categories of curves" are categories of commutative group schemes (178-184); SA19-6's places 195-208 include 203-208, which are Tate pairings and local symbols (SA19-1, SA19-2); SA19-3's places on cote 43 (2-9, 94, 106-107, ...) come from the Pro notes' comparisons with Oda: of them only the margins of 133 (α_p subgroups, F and V, self-duality of the Jacobian) touch Dieudonné theory, and 2-9 are number-field class field theory; SA19-11/12/20's places in "cote 44" (scans 10-54) are pages of cotes 16, 47 and 54 in the shared package: cote 44 has nine scans.
